subject: Creativity
title: Synesthesia and Music: When You See Sound in Color
description: A micro-lesson that makes Synesthesia and Music: When You See Sound in Color usable.

hook.text: Pharrell Williams sees music in colors. Duke Ellington saw D major as blue.

buildup.text: Synesthesia cross-wires the senses — sounds trigger colors, numbers have textures, letters have colors.

discovery.text: About 4% of people have synesthesia. Musicians are overrepresented — the condition may enhance musical memory.

twist.text: Scriabin composed a 'color symphony' — Prometheus: The Poem of Fire — with a part for a light organ onstage.

climax.text: Non-synesthetes can develop weak cross-sensory associations through training.

punchline.text: For some musicians, every note paints a color. Their ears literally see.

quiz.question: What is synesthesia?
options: A neurological condition where senses cross-wire
